svg.text: How TOD Copilot computes each statistic
Recorded data with provenance, measured once when the plan is built, then turned into every scoreboard and target number by pure functions.

g.text: Inputs: recorded data, each value with its provenance
backend/data/providers/ · the resolver takes the first provider that covers the locale
annual kWh per kW at the locale

svg.text: agents measure once, when the plan is built
walk_m[target]: metres to park · clinic · grocery · frequent stop
sites (pursue · watch · pass · reserve) and capital stacks
target = the building (conversion) or first parcel (new build)
in plan = pursue + watch sites · funded = pursue only
homes_by_target: each in-plan site's homes on its target
every constant: value · unit · source_url · note
keys named in mono on each card below; the UI shows
them on hover from each score's factor_keys

g.text: The statistics: scoreboard and target bars
Σ homes of in-plan sites (pursue + watch)
floor = FAR × lot, or lot × coverage × stories
efficiency ÷ unit sqft (mixed use × share; hotel 0)
Σ affordable_units of the capital stacks
a slider re-price keeps the site's count
they rent at the affordable rent in the NOI
share of new homes with a park, clinic AND
grocery all within the walk threshold
per amenity: % of new homes within reach of each
Green space counts as a park (walk 0 / new park)
only if its open area ≥ min_park_area_sqft
households = new homes whose nearest frequent
stop (existing or planned) is within the walk
Reuse: Σ rentable sqft of in-plan conversions
homes given up to the slider or a park tile
omitted when the plan has no solar yield
new homes on targets whose centroid lies in
a FEMA high-risk (SFHA) zone ÷ new homes
target 0 %; a rise reads red (lower is better)
the only target with a fixed goal; the others
compare to existing conditions and the
no factors: FEMA NFHL data only

svg.text: Every number comes from pure functions in backend/models/; every constant from backend/data/factors.yaml with a source. No LLM computes or edits a statistic.

Meeting mode: each slider move or tile (homes, park, stop, convert) is an Edit; rescore() replays the edits on the plan, shortens walks to new parks and stops by straight line × walk_detour_factor, and re-runs score_plan in <300 ms.
